title: Google Search kicks off the NFL season with Live Game Feeds and fantasy football advice
snippet: Tonight’s game between the New England Patriots and the Seattle Seahawks isn’t just a Super Bowl LX rematch — it’s also the official start of the 2026 NFL season. Google has invested pretty heavily in football over the past few years through YouTube TV, but today, it’s giving Search some big improvements to make following the season a little easier. more…
fullText:
Tonight’s game between the New England Patriots and the Seattle Seahawks isn’t just a Super Bowl LX rematch — it’s also the official start of the 2026 NFL season. Google has invested pretty heavily in football over the past few years through YouTube TV, but today, it’s giving Search some big improvements to make following the season a little easier.

Google is adding a Live Game Feed to search, which allows fans and spectators alike to follow along with game developments as they unfold on the field. Any active game will show a “Live” icon in search, and selecting that option shows a recap of what’s happened so far alongside a “dynamic timeline featuring play-by-play updates, top social commentary, key video highlights, and AI-powered insights.” This sounds quite a bit like Google’s alternative to something like Apple’s (truly excellent) sports app, though we’ll have to see how it performs in action first.

Meanwhile, Search is also getting a new carousel display that shows other ongoing games whenever you search for a specific matchup, alongside a stats page that shows player-specific performance like rushing yards, sacks, and YAC, with favorability metrics on their way. Finally, Google has tuned AI Mode to assist with your fantasy football lineup, supporting Yahoo Fantasy and Sleeper account sync directly for real-time suggestions ahead of kickoff on Sunday.

Google’s new carousel view in Search is rolling out to all users globally on mobile. Live Game Feed is available in the US in English and currently supports NFL games, with a broader expansion and plans to add collegiate teams coming later this month. Fantasy football advice in AI Mode is, similarly, only available for English-language users in the US.

title: The iPhone Duo is actually a software story
snippet: Good morning, how did you sleep? Me, I had trouble until I started counting the number of times Apple used the word “AI” in its keynote (it was 41). In my dream, I was inundated with Elizabeth Holmes deepfakes and memes, which startled me awake. Good morning, how did you sleep? Me, I had trouble until I started counting the number of times Apple used the word “AI” in its keynote (it was 41). In my dream, I was inundated with Elizabeth Holmes deepfakes and memes, which startled me awake. As I lay in bed, I calmed down by reading about how AI will “kill us all by the end of the decade,” and then I got up and helped ChatGPT do my kids’ homework. Such a great day.

As a reminder, Inbox is the tech newsletter that goes beyond the news cycle. We cover the most important 9to5Google stories from the last couple of days along with a few highlights from around the web. We publish every Tuesday and Thursday, and if you like what you read, please subscribe.

Inbox is written by Daniel Bader. Read previous issues here, and then catch up with Ben Schoon’s excellent Weekender column.

⭐️ Starred

Today’s main story is, of course, Apple’s “Surprise and Shine” event, which debuted two new iPhone 18 Pros, two new Apple Watches, an updated pair of AirPods at a lower price, and a foldable called the iPhone Duo.

	

As predicted (and pre-empted), the iPhone Duo is a book-style foldable slightly wider and shorter than the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8. Apple uses a combination of flexible plastic and thin layers of titanium sandwiched between the OLED panel, and claims that the crease is basically undetectable, though we’ll have to see how well that claim holds up over time. Curiously, Apple has also resurrected the under-display camera, which was a mainstay of Samsung’s Fold line until it disappeared in the Fold 7, as well as Apple Pencil support, which Samsung also dropped in the same generation.

To the credit of Samsung, Oppo, Honor, and even Google, the iPhone Duo does not appear to be dramatically superior to the latest book-style foldables; it matches the latest Pixel Folds’ IP68 water and dust resistance rating (that degrades over time); it relies on a side-mounted fingerprint sensor for authentication over the more convenient Face ID; it only has two cameras, and they lack the upgraded features of the Pro models; and at 254 grams, it’s heavier than practically any other foldable out there today.

What I find more compelling than the hardware is how Apple designed iOS to ostensibly work better with a foldable. Watching the demos, you can immediately see the care that went into the transitions between main and internal displays, and the changes that make the software easier to use with one hand. And while older apps may look funky until they’re updated, Apple has traditionally had better luck than Google convincing (or forcing) developers to adapt their apps to new form factors.

With iOS 27.1, which will be released alongside the iPhone Duo in October, developers will be able to target the foldable in app updates. Apple is banking on the fact that this larger canvas will tempt developers with new ways to earn money, a flywheel that has rewarded the company handsomely over the past 18 years. And hopefully the new attention paid to Apple’s entry will push reluctant developers to consider doing the same for their Android apps — though I’m not holding my breath. 

More from 9to5Mac: Hands-on with the foldable iPhone Duo

✉️ Inbox

Hands-on: Honor’s Robot Phone is probably the coolest phone you still can’t buy. Straight from the IFA floor, Andrew goes hands-on with the most bizarre phone of 2026.

Xiaomi 18 Fold goes on sale with full specs and a Galaxy Z Fold 8 comparison. Xiaomi timed its iPhone Duo competitor perfectly or poorly depending on how you look at it. The phone is intriguing in its own right, with Xiaomi’s first home-grown SoC and a huge 200MP main camera.

Samsung’s Privacy Display and TriFold merge in the Huawei Mate XT2. Samsung may have abandoned the tri-fold category, so Huawei is just stealing its best ideas.

Oppo confirms Find X10 Pro Max and its triple 200MP camera setup will launch this month. Another big release for massive cameras, the Find X10 Pro Max follows the ridiculously well-endowed Find X9 Ultra, which our Ben Schoon called “simply stunning” in his review.

Two Galaxy S27 models will get Samsung’s Privacy Display, not just the Ultra. We’re still doing this, huh?

Hands-on: Orbitkey elevated its time-tested key organizer with a built-in Google Find Hub tracker. As someone who loses his keys all the time, this product just makes sense.

Pebblebee’s latest Android Find Hub trackers have bright neon colors, available today

Google Find Hub update brings new ‘Remembered’ tab with Gemini

Boox Picco is exceptionally tiny for an e-reader, but it parts ways with Android and third-party apps. I am an avowed fan of tiny e-readers, and I am also a Boox Palma 2 owner, so I’ll definitely be picking this up when it debuts in November.

Arm’s new CPU cores and GPUs for Android chips promise ‘desktop-class’ games, more AI power. This is the part where I joke about how excited I am to play a ray-traced version of Candy Crush or something, but Arm genuinely knocked it out of the park with this release.

Google Find Hub update brings new ‘Remembered’ tab with Gemini. I cannot wait to abuse the heck out of this feature.

Google Messages rolls out Keep Notes integration on Android. 

Google Search kicks off the NFL season with Live Game Feeds and fantasy football advice. Go Bills!

Today in bugs, bug fixes, and shutdowns:

Google Maps speedometer disappears on Android Auto for some, traffic data still missing too

Google Messages slowly rolling out fix for bug that randomly sends old texts to other people

Samsung is shutting down ‘Quick Measure’ and ‘AR Doodle’ apps for Galaxy phones

Google Pixel Tablet has been discontinued, out of stock everywhere

🍎 Etc.

Apple didn’t just introduce a foldable iPhone yesterday. There was also the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, and the AirPods 5.

With the Duo stealing much of the spotlight, it may be easy to overlook the other products, but it’s worth sticking with them for a minute. The iPhones, for instance, feature an upgraded main sensor with a variable aperture, a spec that Samsung adopted with the Galaxy S9 and abandoned two years later. Apple’s implementation offers four stops of range (f/1.48, f/1.8, f/2.8, and f/4.0), which are cycled through automatically depending on the environment. I’m not sure how much real-world impact it will have, but the technology has likely come a long way in the past few years, so I’m cautiously optimistic.

Perhaps more interesting is that the iPhone 18 Pro is the first in Apple’s flagship lineup to do away with Qualcomm modems, a change seven years in the making. The C2, which is also in the Duo, is Apple’s first chip to support mmWave in the US, which is required for Verizon’s network. (Oddly, the iPhone 18 Pro Max retains its Qualcomm modem, perhaps because it performs better and can fit into the larger housing.)

The new Apple Watch’s most notable feature may be its most controversial: inside its overarching Audio Intelligence announcement are two features, Live Rewind and Siri Recap, that create transcriptions or summaries of recent interactions. While Apple is quick to point out that no audio data is uploaded to its servers, nor stored permanently on the watch, the reality is that this feature enables surreptitious recording of everyday conversations without consent.

The AirPods 5 is low-key interesting, not because of any particular upgrade but because it’s the only product in Apple’s entire lineup that received a price drop.

This section has some of our favorite stuff from around the internet. Great videos, weird memes, fun reads, recommended apps, whatever. Send us your recommendations!

Watch me and Will Sattelberg talk endlessly about the insane You Can See Everything trailer before dovetailing into a conversation about repairable tech with Fairphone CTO, Chandler Hatton. 

Afterwards, if you still have any brain cells left, you should watch this Metroid Ravenous trailer, which I’ve already seen half a dozen times, and then spend some time with Playdate Season 3, which drops in October.

🎙️ Quotations

I asked the 9to5Google editors to sum up their thoughts on yesterday’s Apple event.

This event really cemented Apple as just another player in the industry, if it wasn’t already. A Pro-tier iPhone leaning on AI tricks as the bulk of its pitch? A foldable that pulls from nearly a decade’s worth of other companies’ devices without bringing much new to the table? What was even new on the Watch Series 12 besides that awful new brown color? Whatever spark of creativity Apple once carried — even from an Android user’s perspective — has been long gone for a while now, but this is the first event where I really felt a burning sense of boredom in the pit of my stomach.

– Will Sattelberg, Senior Writer and Podcaster

The iPhone Duo was the highlight for me; Apple’s entrance to the foldable market was inevitable, and it was fairly well done.

I’m wary of things like the side-oriented UI changes to iOS and the glossy dot in the middle of a matte inner display, but Apple’s usual level of polish has me intrigued. Not enough to drop $2,000 on a device that runs an OS I absolutely loathe, though, especially seeing as Apple didn’t show off much that actually changes the game in terms of using a foldable. The most revolutionary addition was that neat animation when transitioning between displays. For now, I’m still loving my Fold 8.

– Ben Schoon, Senior Editor

Apple did in fact “just walk in” and possibly figure out foldables. That or the reality distortion field was upgraded.

Anyway, I’m personally interested in the Apple Pencil support for the iPhone Duo, while I’m very eager to see how the new sidebar that incorporates status bar icons and the dock feels on the Duo’s cover screen. Ignoring third-party launchers that you have to install yourself, this might be the biggest change in smartphone UX for a bit.

– Abner Li, Editor-in-Chief

No matter how you feel about the iPhone Duo as a device, it’s finally good to see competition begin to heat up for phones that function beyond the range of the smartphones we’ve been using for the over a decade. Unfortunately, that competition is also expensive, just like the Galaxy Z Fold 8 series and the Pixel 11 Pro Fold. Not entirely unexpected, but a nudging reminder of where technology’s economy is right now. I, for one, am excited to see how the iPhone Duo works in the same tests we throw Android foldables through. If the Duo UX looks as good as Apple’s pre-recorded event makes it out to be, there might be plenty to look forward to for both Apple and Android. And who knows, maybe the iPhone Duo 2 won’t be nearly $2,000.

– Andrew Romero, Senior Editor

After seeing the Duo in the hands of the public, it seems like Apple isn’t magically reinventing the foldable after all.

Apple’s take on foldable software is fun, with lots of good hardware choices that will hopefully positively influence Android foldables. But overall, it hasn’t addressed any huge problems that existing foldables aren’t already dealing with.

– Jordan Floyd, Video Producer

title: Report: iPhone Duo could give Apple a 25% share of foldable market in 2026
snippet: A new TrendForce report says the iPhone Duo is expected to capture 24,8% of the foldable smartphone market in 2026 alone, countering a 20% slump in the segment. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
A new TrendForce report says the iPhone Duo is expected to capture 24,8% of the foldable smartphone market in 2026 alone, countering a 20% slump in the segment. Here are the details.

iPhone Duo expected to ship 5 million units by the end of 2026

Following yesterday’s announcement of the iPhone Duo, TrendForce published a report today predicting that Apple will capture 24,8% of the foldable smartphone segment by the end of the year.

TrendForce expects Apple to ship 5 million units of the iPhone Duo in 2026, helping offset a segment-wide slowdown due to “sharp increases in component costs”:

TrendForce forecasts global foldable smartphone shipments of approximately 20.2 million units in 2026, up just 0.5% YoY. Excluding Apple, combined shipments from Android brands are expected to reach only around 15.2 million units, down more than 20% YoY.

The report notes that Samsung is still poised to lead the market with 7.1 million units shipped for the year and 35.1% market share, and expects Huawei to match Apple’s 5 million units shipped and 24.8% share.

TrendForce goes on to analyze some of Apple’s hardware choices for the iPhone Duo, including the trade-offs the company made to achieve its final design:

Apple has omitted a dedicated periscope telephoto camera to minimize thickness and conserve internal space. Instead, the 48 MP main camera provides 2x optical-quality zoom, while a side-mounted Touch ID sensor replaces Face ID. These choices highlight the trade-offs that foldable smartphones continue to face among device thickness, camera capabilities, biometric components, and battery space.

TrendForce rounds out the report by looking ahead at the foldable segment, suggesting that “deeper integration of AI and multitasking interfaces with the larger foldable display could transform the device from a hardware differentiator into a new interface for AI applications.”

title: Proxima Fusion bets €140M on a critical fusion ingredient dominated by Asian suppliers
snippet: Proxima Fusion said Wednesday it plans to build a €140 million ($162.6 million) factory to produce fusion-grade high-temperature superconducting (HTS) tape, which will provide the startup with key component to its reactor design.
fullText:
In Brief

Posted:

11:38 AM PDT · September 10, 2026

Image Credits:Proxima Fusion

		

							

											
									

					

	

Proxima Fusion is betting on a critical ingredient for its fusion reactors: superconducting tape.

Proxima Fusion said Wednesday it plans to build a €140 million ($162.6 million) factory to produce fusion-grade high-temperature superconducting (HTS) tape, which will provide the startup with key component to its reactor design.

The move comes months after Proxima raised €411 million in a round that catapulted the company up the ranks of the best-funded fusion startups. The Germany-based fusion startup plans to use a mix of public and private funding to complete the factory, with the state of Lower Saxony chipping in €21 million. 

Proxima will use HTS tape to generate powerful magnetic fields to contain the plasma required to spark fusion reactions. 

The startup’s demonstration plant will use 20,000 kilometers of HTS tape, while its commercial power plant will need twice as much. Today, the vast majority of HTS tape is made in China and Japan.

HTS tape emerged a little over a decade ago as one of the fundamental breakthroughs that enabled the current generation of fusion power startups. Because it can generate strong magnetic fields at relatively high temperatures, HTS tape enables smaller and more efficient reactor designs.

While fusion power is expected to consume a large portion of the world’s HTS tape production, other companies like Veir are using it to boost the efficiency and power density of data centers.

title: This might be iPhone 18 Pro’s best camera feature for most users
snippet: iPhone 18 Pro packs lots of camera upgrades (great rundown here), with the tentpole addition being variable aperture. But there’s one other Main camera change that users like me might deem their favorite. more…
fullText:
iPhone 18 Pro packs lots of camera upgrades (great rundown here), with the tentpole addition being variable aperture. But there’s one other Main camera change that users like me might deem their favorite.

iPhone 18 Pro’s new f/1.48 lens could prove popular for the average non-‘pro’ user

As impressive as Apple’s new iPhone Duo foldable is, when it comes to camera features, it’s a clear loser to the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max (see our iPhone Duo-iPhone 18 Pro comparison here).

Not only does iPhone Duo lack a Telephoto camera, but its Main camera also misses out on the improvements coming to iPhone 18 Pro.

For a rundown of iPhone 18 Pro camera upgrades, I recommend my colleague Ben’s piece here.

As I’ve been thinking about the new camera system, many of the changes appear meant for users that are more “pro” than me. All of the manual ‘Pro controls’ iPhone 18 Pro offers intimidate me, and I don’t expect to ever use them. Even the tentpole variable aperture feature feels a bit over my head, though I’m glad it can work automatically.

Relevant background: I have zero training in photography outside of a single ‘Today at Apple’ class I took years ago. But of course, I love to take photos with my iPhone.

And the iPhone 18 Pro camera change I’m most intrigued by is something highlighted by The Verge. Antonio G. Di Benedetto writes:

I think the real star feature of the iPhone 18 Pro’s camera is its f/1.48 maximum aperture…People love bokeh. Last year’s Pro iPhone cameras had an f/1.7 aperture, and now being at f/1.48, the 18 Pro camera should work better in low-light as well as have a slightly shallower depth of field. Will f/1.48 be a huge difference in bokeh from f/1.7? Probably not. It’s likely to have depth of field that’s just a smidge shallower — but that’s the look that people often like.

I speak from experience here, as I usually shoot on full-frame cameras and one of my go-to lenses is a 50mm with an f/1.2 maximum aperture. A lens that fast, with depth of field that shallow gives a unique look that’s easy to overuse, but it almost never fails that people swoon when I take their portrait using that lens — with that blurry, “dreamy” blur isolating them from the background. The f/1.48 of the iPhone 18 Pro is obviously not going to compare to an f/1.2 on full-frame, but f/1.2 and similarly wide apertures on big sensors is the look that people often want to emulate. It’s the whole reason Portrait Modes on smartphones came into being in the first place.

I haven’t used an iPhone 18 Pro yet. But I wouldn’t be surprised if the new f/1.48 aperture proves a hit among users like me.

Most iPhone 18 Pro buyers will, I suspect, never touch any of the custom manual controls. But if their everyday photos offer more natural, “dreamy” bokeh—even if just a little bit—then the iPhone 18 Pro camera could be beloved for that reason alone.

title: Google signs its biggest rice-methane carbon credit deal with Indian startup Mitti Labs
snippet: The four-year agreement will cover rice farms across three Indian states, reaching about 100,000 hectares at peak delivery.
fullText:
Google has agreed to buy 1 million carbon credits from Indian climate-tech startup Mitti Labs through 2030, in what the companies say is the largest publicly announced deal to date for credits generated from cutting methane emissions in rice farming.

The four-year agreement will cover rice farms across the Indian states of Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana, reaching about 100,000 hectares at peak delivery, Mitti Labs co-founder Xavier Laguarta said in an interview. Financial terms were not disclosed.

The project will pay farmers to adopt practices that reduce how long rice fields remain flooded, cutting methane released during cultivation while also reducing water use. Mitti Labs says the technique can cut methane emissions by about 50% and irrigation water use by about 40% without reducing crop yields.

The deal comes as Google faces the challenge of reaching its goal of going net-zero emissions by 2030 amid investing heavily in artificial-intelligence infrastructure. Its greenhouse gas emissions in 2025 grew 18% year-over-year to about 14.5 million metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent, per its environmental report (PDF) released in June.

Mitti Labs began talks with Google about a year ago, Laguarta told TechCrunch, as the tech company explored adding methane-reduction projects to its carbon-credit portfolio. Google was drawn in part to the project’s water savings and Mitti Labs’ ability to operate at scale, he stated.

The startup’s projects have saved more than 500 billion liters of water over the past two years. The Google deal, Laguarta said, would allow Mitti Labs to expand further, giving it the scale needed to work with large corporate buyers.

Mitti Labs’ Measurement Chamber at a Rice FarmImage Credits:Mitti Labs

“Having Google, one of the most sophisticated buyers in the market with rigorous due diligence processes, is obviously a good signal for us,” Laguarta said, adding that the deal would allow Mitti to scale significantly.

Google’s evaluation included scrutiny of Mitti Labs’ monitoring technology and visits to farms before the companies signed the agreement, Laguarta said. Founded in 2023, the New York- and Bengaluru-based startup has built a GeoAI platform that combines satellite radar imagery with field measurements to remotely track crop growth, soil moisture, and flooding across smallholder farms.

The platform uses synthetic aperture radar imagery from commercial and public satellites, with resolutions ranging from 50 centimeters to 10 meters. Mitti also uses proprietary data collected in the field to train its AI models, Laguarta said.

The credits sold to Google can be issued under either Gold Standard or Isometric, two carbon-credit certification bodies, Laguarta said. He added that the projects undergo independent third-party verification as part of the certification process before credits are issued.

In addition to Google, Mitti Labs works with customers including carbon marketplace Cool Effect, rice producer Ebro Foods, and agricultural company Syngenta. Laguarta told TechCrunch that the Google agreement is Mitti Labs’ largest offtake deal to date.

Mitti Labs currently works with more than 100,000 farmers and aims to have millions of farmers by 2030. The Google deal, Laguarta said, would help the startup move toward that goal by allowing it to expand its projects.

A majority of the revenue from the startup’s projects goes to farming communities, Laguarta noted. He declined to disclose how much farmers participating in the Google project would receive, however.

While the Google project is limited to India, Mitti Labs plans to launch operations in the Philippines later this year and expand into Indonesia and other Southeast Asian markets in 2027.

Laguarta sees room for the market to grow as more companies look to agricultural projects to tackle methane emissions. About 150 million farmers grow rice across India, Southeast Asia, and China, he told TechCrunch.

The deal with Mitti Labs is not Google’s first carbon-removal investment in India. In January 2025, the Mountain View, California-headquartered company partnered with Gurugram-based Varaha to buy 100,000 tons of carbon credits. That was Google’s first large-scale purchase of carbon removal credits in the country and the largest involving biomass-produced biochar.

Google is also turning to clean-energy projects in India to address its supply-chain emissions. The company has signed an agreement tied to a 150-megawatt solar project in Rajasthan, taking its contracted solar capacity with ReNew in the state to 300 megawatts.

title: The New AppleCare One Family Plan Will Cover Every Apple Gadget in Your House
snippet: For the cost of a new iPad mini every year, AppleCare will cover all your devices.
fullText:
Apple has a new device protection plan for families for $50 per month. And it doesn’t matter how many devices your family has — they’re all covered.

Apple announced the AppleCare One Family plan at its Surprise and Shine event on Wednesday. The plan will be available starting Sept. 14. You can find it in your device’s settings. 

Apple’s website says you’ll get all of the AppleCare Plus benefits, like unlimited repairs from accidents like drops and spills and 24/7 priority support from Apple experts. It also includes theft and loss coverage up to twice in a year for iPhones, iPads and Apple Watches.  

These products are covered under the AppleCare One Family plan based on Apple’s website:

AirPods

Apple TV

Apple Vision Pro 

Apple Watch

HomePod

iPad

iPhone 

Mac 

Watch

Studio displays

Apple’s family Apple Care plan covers all devices for up to six people. And if you decide to add new products, like the iPhone Duo, those are automatically added without extra fees. The AppleCare One plan for individuals only covers up to three products for $20 per month, and any additional device is an extra $6 per month. So, if every member of a family of four has an iPad, Apple Watch and iPhone, that’s 12 devices covered for $50 a month (or $600 annually) compared to each person getting the AppleCare One plan for $20 per month — totaling $80 monthly or $960 annually. That’s $300 in savings.

The AppleCare Plus and AppleCare One plans are still available, and pricing depends on the devices you need to protect.

Apple has a few other bundling services worth considering if you’re looking to save on its services. Apple One’s family plan costs $28 per month for up to six people. It includes 200GB of iCloud storage, Apple TV Plus, Apple Arcade and Apple Music.

title: Google Maps speedometer disappears on Android Auto for some, traffic data still missing too
snippet: Android Auto users are reporting an issue where the Google Maps speedometer, available for mere months, is randomly vanishing. more…
fullText:
Android Auto users are reporting an issue where the Google Maps speedometer, available for mere months, is randomly vanishing.

Back in July, Google Maps on Android Auto finally started rolling out support for a live speedometer while navigating. This was alongside showing speed limits. It started more broadly rolling out later that month, but still hasn’t rolled out to everyone.

Now, in fact, we’re looking at the exact opposite happening. A number of users have reported on Reddit that the speedometer has suddenly vanished on Android Auto. It’s not a particularly widespread issue, it seems, but the rollout hasn’t expanded to all users in the first place. This is alongside traffic patterns, which are still missing for a number of users after breaking in late August. 

We’ve also noticed continued reports of Android Auto missing its signal indicator, an ongoing bug for months at this point.

	

Google rolls out new Android Auto updates on a pretty regular basis, along with Maps, but these isolated issues just don’t seem to be going away. Leave a comment below if you’re running into these problems.

title: OpenAI releases ChatGPT Images 2.5 with ‘sharper details’ and ‘more precise editing’
snippet: In April, OpenAI released upgraded image generation technology with ChatGPT Images 2. Five months later, the company is releasing an enhanced version, ChatGPT Images 2.5. more…
fullText:
In April, OpenAI released upgraded image generation technology with ChatGPT Images 2. Five months later, the company is releasing an enhanced version, ChatGPT Images 2.5. 

ChatGPT Images 2 was a notable leap over the company’s earlier image generation tools.

It added 2K resolution output, multiple aspect ratio support, and the ability to use web research for up-to-date information. Images 2 also added non-Latin language expertise and two intelligence levels: Instant and Thinking.

The latest Images 2.5 version touts “sharper details, faster generation, more precise editing, and better tools for creating and sharing.”

“Images 2.5 produces more natural lighting and richer textures, is better at preserving the subjects in your reference photos, and follows editing instructions more reliably across multiple turns,” OpenAI says.

“We’ve also reduced image generation latency by up to 50% compared with Images 2.0, so you can generate images and refine your concepts more quickly.”

Additionally, the company details a new “Sketch” feature that enables drawing directly in ChatGPT. This can be used as a reference for image generation. Plus OpenAI is introducing templates for popular image formats, prompt sharing for others to try your ideas related to image-gen, and more.

Additionally, OpenAI is releasing two versions of Images 2.5 for developers to build around in their apps. GPT-Image-2.5 Flare and GPT-Image-2.5 Sunburt will be available through OpenAI’s API:

GPT‑Image‑2.5 Flare brings the same improvements in quality, editing, and speed to the API and is the default choice for most applications, delivering higher-quality images than GPT‑Image‑2 at 50% lower latency. It’s well suited to everything from creator and social content to product experiences, visual search, rapid image prototyping, and high-volume generation.

GPT‑Image‑2.5 Sunburst is built for premium visual workflows that benefit from tighter control across edits. Use it for creative and editing workflows like production-ready campaign creative or polished product imagery.

title: macOS 27 Golden Gate: Here are Apple’s full release notes
snippet: Apple has announced that macOS 27 Golden Gate will ship to all users next Monday, September 14. Here are Apple’s official release notes for macOS 27. more…
fullText:
Apple has announced that macOS 27 Golden Gate will ship to all users next Monday, September 14. Here are Apple’s official release notes for macOS 27.

Apple’s official macOS 27 release notes now available

Today alongside shipping its RC (release candidate) updates, Apple published full release notes for iOS 27 and also for macOS 27 Golden Gate.

Here are the full, unedited macOS 27 release notes:

Experience the new Siri AI

Introducing Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri powered by Apple Intelligence that’s more personal, more capable, and more conversational. It is integrated into Spotlight, so you can search for answers about almost any topic right from where you already search for things across your system. It can draw on personal context to find things across your messages, mail, photos, and more. And it can get things done across your apps, just by asking. Revisit and resume past conversations in the new dedicated Siri app, synced with iCloud across your Apple devices. Siri AI is rolling out to users, and you can get started by turning it on in Settings.

Take action on what’s onscreen

With Visual Intelligence, you can select a window of your screen and Siri can answer questions or take action with what’s onscreen, like adding events to your calendar. You can access Visual Intelligence with a dedicated keyboard shortcut — Command-Shift-Space.

Powerful new ways to edit photos

Use intelligent photo editing tools to reframe a photo after it’s been taken with Spatial Reframing or expand your shot with the Extend tool. And enhancements to Clean Up let you remove distractions with better quality and more realistic infill, even when the scene is complex.

New tools to browse in Safari

Automatically group your tabs into topics, so related pages are easier to find. With Notify Me, Safari can monitor pages for changes like price drops or restocks and alert you when it’s time to act. Describe an Extension lets you use natural language to create custom extensions, like adding a button to save your favorite recipes.

Easily create Shortcuts using natural language

With Describe a Shortcut, you can automate daily tasks with a simple description and all of the required steps are assembled on your behalf. For example, you can describe a shortcut to automatically text your partner when you’re headed home from work with an estimated arrival time based on traffic.

Even more refined design

Updates to Liquid Glass improve readability, and a new slider lets you customize how it looks, from ultra-clear to fully tinted. Uniform toolbars, edge-to-edge sidebars, and more detailed app icons further elevate the design.

New child safety features

Powerful new parental controls help parents more easily manage what content their children can see, who they can communicate with, and when they have access to apps. Ask to Browse requires kids to request permission before visiting any new website in Safari. Communication Safety expands its protections to help keep conversations safe. Time Allowances gives parents more flexible ways to manage the time kids spend in apps across categories, and offers guidance based on expert research that’s tailored to a child’s age. Schedules help manage which apps kids have access to at different times of the day and across the week.

A more responsive and delightful experience

An expansive set of improvements make your Mac even faster, more reliable, and easier to use. Better search in Spotlight and Mail helps you find what you’re looking for with greater ease. AirDrop Transfers and network file browsing happen faster. And many more improvements make your day-to-day use more enjoyable.

For information on the security content of Apple software updates, please visit: support.apple.com/100100.

Some features may not be available in all regions or on all Apple devices. To learn more, please visit: apple.com/macos/feature-availability.

Usage limits may apply for some Apple Intelligence features, including but not limited to Siri AI, Intelligent Photo Editing Tools, Image Playground and AFM 3 Cloud models in Shortcuts. To learn more please visit: apple.com/apple-intelligence.

Software updates, like this one, add new features and improvements that may affect performance and/or battery life. To learn more, please visit: support.apple.com/125039.

title: Apple addresses iPhone Duo copycats
snippet: John Ternus, Apple CEO, holds an iPhone Duo at the launch event. | Bloomberg via Getty Images Apple was far from the first company to announce a passport-shaped folding phone this year, but that doesn't mean it wasn't copied. fullText:
Thomas Ricker

 

is a deputy editor and Verge co-founder with a passion for human-centric cities, e-bikes, and life as a digital nomad. He’s been a tech journalist for 20 years.

Apple was far from the first company to announce a passport-shaped folding phone this year, but that doesn’t mean it wasn’t copied. As my colleague Dom Preston already explained, it’s almost impossible to keep product development secret when Apple and its competitors all share the same global suppliers.

Apple’s new CEO John Ternus and head of marketing Greg ‘Joz’ Joswiak addressed the topic during an interview with TechRadar’s Lance Ulanoff and Mark Spoonauer of Tom’s Guide.

“People knew through leaks that we were working on a foldable,” said Joz. “Unfortunately, they got the aspect ratio, and a lot of coincidental instances of people finding that an interesting aspect ratio.” By “people,” Joz means Samsung, Huawei, and Xiaomi who all announced wide foldables ahead of Apple.

What did remain a secret is the folding nano-texture display unique to the iPhone Duo. “What I’m super proud of — we kept it secret,” said Joz. “We put the extra security on it. We didn’t talk about it to anybody.”

The whole interview is worth a watch. Ternus’ boyish enthusiasm is a refreshing change from the more measured Tim Cook, signaling his roots as a hands-on engineer. You can see it when describing his first interaction with a prototype of the display. “Oh this is it, this is what I want,” he said, eagerly grinning.

The new head of Apple is clearly a product guy, just like its mercurial founder.

The Last First: Winter K2 premieres October 2

On October 2, Apple TV will debut The Last First: Winter K2, a revealing documentary that “tells a complex, harrowing and moving story” of extreme mountain climbing, and currently holds a rare 100% Rotten Tomatoes score.

Apple TV first announced it had acquired the global rights to The Last First: Winter K2 earlier this year, mentioning that it was a Sundance Film Festival selection documentary.

In “The Last First: Winter K2,” Amir Bar-Lev tells a complex, harrowing and moving story that takes an unflinching look at the industry of extreme mountain climbing and its changing culture. Focusing on a 2021 expedition, this documentary follows Icelander John Snorri Sigurjónsson and the Pakistani father-son team of Ali and Sajid Sadpara, a party of mountaineers who set out to be the first to summit K2 in the winter, when the mountain’s conditions are the cruelest. The men soon find themselves sharing the treacherous ascent with influencer climbers and their film crews, commercial expedition clients, and a Nepalese team no longer content to help Westerners achieve mountaineering glory. “The Last First: Winter K2” takes us to the icy heights and unpredictable weather of K2 and reveals a surprising and layered story — one of strategy and determination, class and caste, money and power — all under life-and-death circumstances.

title: The Galaxy Z Fold 8 needs battery banks that actually fit; iPhone Duo might help
snippet: Magnetic battery banks aren’t everyone’s cup of tea, but it’s hard to argue with the convenience factor they deliver. Samsung’s camera design already makes these difficult on Galaxy devices, but Galaxy Z Fold 8 only makes matters worse with a short form factor that leaves battery banks hanging way over the edge. iPhone Duo might help matters here, but the same old problem remains. more…
fullText:
Magnetic battery banks aren’t everyone’s cup of tea, but it’s hard to argue with the convenience factor they deliver. Samsung’s camera design already makes these difficult on Galaxy devices, but Galaxy Z Fold 8 only makes matters worse with a short form factor that leaves battery banks hanging way over the edge. iPhone Duo might help matters here, but the same old problem remains.

The Qi ring on Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 is very low on any already-short frame, which leaves magnetic wallets and battery banks well out of place on the foldable, hanging down below the bottom of the device. It’s a problem begging for a solution, and one that other wide foldables are also going to run into.

Is the iPhone Duo the solution to Samsung’s problem?

Not just yet. The iPhone Duo is bringing about a new wave of smaller Qi2 battery banks to fit the short and stout form factor. BMX just launched one of the first models with a solid-state battery specifically designed to fit the Duo. It has a kickstand ring and a little display to show battery percentage, with 5,000 mAh of power and a fit that doesn’t hang below the bottom edge of Apple’s first foldable.

	

I was hoping this would work on the Galaxy Z Fold 8, but BMX tells 9to5Google that this power bank won’t fit on Samsung’s device due to the camera. Foiled again!

Samsung’s camera design continues to be a problem here, which is why it’s nice that Samsung might be moving to something new on some of its Galaxy S27 devices. But, in the meantime, it remains a problem for existing users.

While BMX says the battery bank won’t fit perfectly on the Fold 8, it’s likely still a major improvement. The $80 power bank is available for purchase now, and it probably won’t be the last battery designed for the Duo and, in turn, a better fit for the Fold 8.

title: Don’t Sleep on Apple’s Audio Intelligence. It Reveals a Lot About Where We’re Headed
snippet: Commentary: Apple’s new memory tools are a sign of how tech companies are pushing into a new wave of AI wearables, and glasses are likely next.
fullText:
The first five minutes of John Ternus’ first keynote as Apple CEO weren’t a product unveiling or a recap of Apple’s history. Instead, they were a redefinition of the iPhone as an “intelligent personal hub.”

Of all the devices Apple makes, the iPhone doesn’t need to be described or explained to anyone. But this new framing of it as a hub not only set up the debut of the foldable, category-straddling iPhone Duo, an iPhone/iPad hybrid of sorts — it also suggested an AI-infused wearable device future that Apple’s already dipping its toes into.

	

			

Of all the things Apple announced during its “Surprise and shine” event this week, the one that hit hardest for me wasn’t the Duo. It was the reveal of Audio Intelligence, a new AI-powered assistive toolset that will live on the latest Apple Watches and even a range of recent iPhone models.

Siri will store Recaps of conversations had previously, provided the always-listening feature is turned on.Apple/Screenshot by CNET

Audio Intelligence: A memory-keeping tool, or a listening device?

Audio Intelligence listens. And in listening, it can make memories. Or recall things. Or, in a sense, act like the sort of AI-enabled wearables I’ve been trying in various forms over the last few years. Live Rewind can check back on things said up to 15 seconds ago, while Siri Recap ambiently summarizes and transcribes conversations when it’s turned on.

Apple promises that Audio Intelligence is encrypted and that no actual audio recordings are saved. But what it does reminds me of Plaud’s AI wearables, or features like the “Conversate” transcription function on the Even Realities G2 smart glasses. Or Looki’s AI conversation summaries.

It’s designed, it seems, to run in the background and record conversations as you’re having them — transcribing them and summarizing them so you can read the text transcriptions later, or on the fly, and available in Siri to search as needed. And if you happen to miss what someone’s saying in a chat, there’s “Live Rewind” that replays the last 15 seconds of a real-life chat, like some real-life version of asking your Apple TV what someone just said on that Netflix show.

Seen here: Meta’s Ray-Bans. Apple’s expected to have its own smart glasses next year.Scott Stein/CNET

A stepping stone for visual intelligence wearables next year

Audio Intelligence also recognizes real-life sounds like sirens or doorbells, something that was already part of Apple’s assistive suite of Apple Watch and AirPod features.

What will it feel like to use Audio Intelligence on an Apple Watch? I don’t know. Maybe like wearing an AI pendant on my wrist. But also, I wonder what Apple is preparing us for next. 

Recaps and summaries equal memories. Audio is easier to record than photos and video. But Visual Intelligence, a camera-based way to use Siri to analyze, translate or remember things that you see, already exists on iPhones, iPads and the Vision Pro, and Apple’s eventual next-gen AirPods are expected to have cameras in them to use Visual Intelligence in the real world — maybe in a very similar way to how Audio Intelligence seems to work on the Apple Watch.

And then there are smart glasses. Apple’s expected to have glasses next year, and the smart glasses already out there lean heavily on AI… and are starting to be feared as privacy-invading gadgets. Meta’s bearing the brunt of that anti-smart-glasses anger now, but will Apple find a way to ease people into feeling like assistive, continuously aware (and perhaps recording) AI devices are helpful, or comfortable, or acceptable? Audio Intelligence feels like one delicate foot into a zone that’s getting more intimate and strange every year.

Apple’s making big privacy claims, but will it help?Apple/Screenshot by CNET

Can Apple convince us it’s safe?

Apple needs to advance its AI to find true assistive uses on glasses, but it also needs to nail down privacy concerns for always-recording wearables. I said this back in June when the debut of the new Siri clearly pointed to a framework for AI wearables and smart glasses to come.

Apple has to start somewhere. And that somewhere looks like Audio Intelligence on the new Apple Watches. And if it works in a way that feels useful and not creepy, then maybe it’s the first part of the next phase of the “intelligent hub” that Ternus’ iPhone ecosystem is heading towards in 2027 and beyond.

		

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Scott Stein
						

						

							Editor at Large						
					

											

								

											I started with CNET reviewing laptops in 2009. Now I explore wearable tech, VR/AR, tablets, gaming and future/emerging trends in our changing world. Other obsessions include magic, immersive theater, puzzles, board games, cooking, improv and the New York Jets. title: Apple Watch Ultra 4 Hands-On: A Closer Look at Its Biggest Upgrades
snippet: Finally a battery worthy of an ultramarathon, better health sensors and a powerful processor that keeps it running.
fullText:
The Apple Watch Ultra 4, which starts at $799, has a new processor and reengineered health sensors that unlock more frequent health measurements, new recovery insights and AI-powered audio tools.

I got to test the Apple Watch Ultra 4 to see some of these new features in action in a demo room at the Steve Jobs Theater after the company’s Surprise and Shine event on Wednesday.

At first glance, the Ultra 4 looked and felt very familiar. But when I flipped it over, the difference was obvious. Compared with the sensor array on my Ultra 3, the back of the Ultra 4 looks almost flower-like, with 32 electrodes resembling the thin petals of a gerbera daisy replacing the previous ring of two. That gives the electrodes more surface area to capture ECG readings. Apple also rearranged the green and infrared LEDs into a new, smaller circular cluster in the middle of the petals with smaller dots.

	

			

Those redesigned sensors, combined with the new S11 processor, allow the Ultra 4 to take heart-rate readings every 5 seconds, compared with roughly every 5 minutes on previous models. The same goes for heart-rate variability, or HRV, which the watch can now measure every 5 minutes instead of just a few times throughout the day. Apple says the increased sampling frequency makes it the most accurate wearable on the market. It also powers a new Readiness score, a measure of how well your body is recovering from exercise during the day.  

The sensors on the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 are different from those on earlier models.Apple/Screenshot by CNET

Unlike many wearables that give you a recovery or readiness score based largely on what happened overnight, Apple’s score changes throughout the day. Because the Ultra 4 samples heart rate and HRV more frequently, Readiness can react in real time as you drain or recharge your body.

I also found a new Daytime toggle in the Vitals app on the watch that lets you view daytime heart rate and HRV alongside the overnight measurements already available in Vitals, like temperature and SpO2. Both features require seven days of data to unlock, so I’ll need at least a week to test them and see whether they align with how I’m feeling, which has often been at odds with what I’ve seen on other devices.

The Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Series 12 are available for preorder and will arrive on Sept. 18. 

Apple/Screenshot by CNET

Your Apple Watch is listening, but not recording

The Ultra 4 and Series 12 also gained new Audio Intelligence features, including one called Live Rewind that lets you jump back and hear the previous 15 seconds of a conversation with just a press of the digital crown. During my live demo, the transcription was spot-on, despite the noisy environment. 

The other AI audio feature is Siri Recap, which lets the watch actively listen and detect conversations throughout the day (or at set times) to generate high-level notes and summaries from meetings or other conversations you may want to revisit. You can trigger a recap manually or schedule one ahead of time. 

Apple says it designed the features so audio isn’t stored and instead only keeps the transcripts you save, which only you can access.  

Read more: I Ran 30 Miles With 5 Smartwatches. Here’s the One You Can Actually Trust

S11 chip absorbs background tasks

The S11 chip is a big part of how the watch pulls this all off without destroying its battery life. It has a dedicated always-on processor that handles background tasks such as heart-rate monitoring and audio processing without constantly waking the main processor.

Apple/Screenshot by CNET

Battery life remains one of the biggest reasons to choose an Ultra over the flagship Series 12. Apple also slightly increased the battery capacity this year, bringing the estimated battery life to roughly 50 hours, up from 42 hours on the Ultra 3.

That’s still nowhere near the weeks of battery life you can get from some Garmin watches. But Apple seems to be making a different trade-off that favors accuracy (via more frequent reads) over saving on battery life.  

Battery trade-offs for endurance athletes 

For endurance athletes, though, the more interesting upgrade is its battery life during workouts.

The Ultra 4 now has two sports-specific low-battery modes meant to keep it tracking for much longer without sacrificing core fitness metrics.

Extended Workout mode: Can track a workout for up to 25 hours by turning off the always-on display and running-form metrics, while keeping GPS and heart-rate tracking at full fidelity.

Max Extended Workout mode: Pushes tracking to as long as 48 hours. GPS still records at 1-second intervals, although it drops from multiband to single-band GPS and heart rate shows a rolling 5-minute average instead of the live metric. The mode also disables custom workouts, alerts and splits, along with certain other metrics.

Apple is essentially letting athletes choose which compromises they’re willing to make depending on how long they need the watch to last.

My take 

The 49mm screen and rugged build are too bulky for me to use the Ultra as my everyday Apple Watch. But the new readiness features, better battery life and more accurate data collection make it tempting for endurance athletes and anyone upgrading from an older Ultra.

Rather than compete head-on with sports watches like Garmin or Coros, Apple is betting that athletes will trade some of that battery life for subscription-free data, high-accuracy tracking and a watch that can now make better use of all that data throughout the day.

title: Amazon makes it easier to buy what you see on Prime Video
snippet: Amazon is expanding shopping integrations across Prime Video, letting viewers discover products tied to thousands of shows, movies, and live sports through X-Ray, its shopping app, and a new Lens-powered “Shop the Scene” feature.
fullText:
Amazon is going to make it easier to shop when you’re watching TV. The retail giant on Thursday announced a series of new features that will allow customers to discover products across thousands of Prime Video titles through integrations with its existing X-Ray experience, which today displays real-time actor bios, character names, soundtrack music, and more. It will also introduce a new way to “shop the scene” using Amazon’s Lens technology, along with other updates.

The changes follow last year’s launch of “Shop the Show,” a second-screen shopping experience available through the Amazon mobile shopping app. Instead of interrupting your viewing experience or displaying product information on-screen, this feature would take you to products tied to a given movie, show, or live sports event when you typed “shop the show” into the Amazon Search app.

Arguably, that feature was easy to miss. These new features will make the product recommendations more prominent and easier to access.

Amazon joins a number of services that are working to integrate shopping suggestions into the viewing experience to create an additional revenue stream. YouTube has long offered creators a merch shelf to hawk their products and offers shoppable connected TV ads. Peacock in 2023 added a Must ShopTV feature that lets viewers buy products that appeared in its content. Roku also offers a way to shop with its remote. Disney has experimented with shoppable TV, including in streaming ads on Disney+, Hulu, and ESPN.

To shop via Amazon’s X-Ray, you’d launch the X-Ray experience as usual by pressing up on the Fire TV remote. You’ll then be able to visit the new Shop tab that will showcase products related to what you’re watching. To make a purchase, you would then open the Amazon Shopping app, which recognizes what’s playing and drops you into a feed synced to that moment, where you can browse the products you like.

The second-screen experience beyond X-Ray has been improved as well. Instead of requiring users to enter the “shop the show” search request, they can just open the Amazon Shopping app while watching a movie or show and be taken to that title’s storefront.

Image Credits:Amazon

They can then tap the image to have Amazon’s visual search technology, Amazon Lens, identify other products inspired by the characters’ outfits, home decor, and other items appearing in the scene. This feature, called “Shop the Scene,” won’t always lead to an exact match; characters are often wearing clothing that Amazon or its sellers don’t stock, including pieces from high-end brands or handmade costumes. But it will at least be a jumping-off point for finding products that could help you achieve a similar look.

The “Shop the Scene” technology is live today on iOS and Android in the U.S. and works with more than 600 titles.

The “Shop the Show” feature in Amazon’s app is expanding from 1,300 titles to more than 8,000 in the U.S. These include Prime Originals, select licensed favorites, and live sports, the retailer notes.

title: Google upgrades all Gemini side panels in Workspace to have the same features
snippet: Gemini in Google Workspace can now “complete complex, cross-app tasks” from whatever app you’re working in. more…
fullText:
Gemini in Google Workspace can now “complete complex, cross-app tasks” from whatever app you’re working in.

Previously, the Gemini side panels found in each Workspace app had capabilities specific to that service: “generating a personalized document with Gemini required being in Docs while building AI-powered spreadsheets required being in Sheets.”

Google is now upgrading each instance of Gemini in Workspace to have the same feature set. This applies to the side panels in Gmail, Drive, Docs, Slides, and Chat. The upgrade is made possible by Workspace Intelligence and deeper app integrations.

For example, you can have Gemini “send an email to my sales team for their review and feedback” from Google Docs instead of needing to be in Gmail. 

	

In Google Chat, you can “find open times, schedule meetings, or resolve calendar conflicts.” Google Tasks also lets you “instantly log a reminder or create a to-do list” from any service.

On the content creation front, example prompts include:

When in Gmail (via the side panel) to create a doc: “Create a strategy brief for this project with goals, milestones and next steps.“

When in Gmail (via the side panel) to create a spreadsheet: “Create a tracker for this project in a new spreadsheet”

When in Docs (via the side panel) to create a deck: “Turn this proposal into an easy to read slide deck for my director using @presentation as a style reference.”

When in Chat (via Ask Gemini in Chat) to create a document: “Create a deck outlining Project Zebra with the latest updates”

When in Drive (via Ask Gemini in Drive) to create a document: “Create a customer insights deck from project Zebra using my project files including sheets, reports, and emails”

This expanded feature set started rolling out this month. For consumers, this is available to subscribers of Google AI Pro (“with the exception of scheduling functionality”) and Google AI Ultra. It’s also coming to:

Business: Standard and Plus

Enterprise: Standard and Plus

Other Editions: Frontline Plus (only for scheduling functionality)

Education Add-ons: Google AI Pro for Education

Other Add-ons: AI Expanded Access

title: tvOS 27 removes a feature that some Apple TV users might miss after updating
snippet: When tvOS 27 is released later this month, Apple TV users will gain an overhauled Podcasts app. The new version includes Apple’s new video podcast streaming technology. fullText:
When tvOS 27 is released later this month, Apple TV users will gain an overhauled Podcasts app. The new version includes Apple’s new video podcast streaming technology.

However, eagle-eyed users may notice that the upcoming software update removes one feature that may be missed after updating: support for shows followed by a URL.

Podcasts on Apple TV 4K gets a big update that removes a niche feature

As mentioned, Apple TV 4K is adding support for streaming HLS-based video podcasts in the Podcasts app in tvOS 27.

This follows the same feature coming to iOS 26.4’s Podcasts app on iPhone and iPad. The Mac also supports HLS video shows in macOS 27 Golden Gate.

But tvOS 27.0 lacks one feature as part of the new version. Shows added with a custom URL, like membership-only feeds for paid podcasts, no longer work on Apple TV 4K’s Podcasts app with tvOS 27.

This is likely a feature oversight or something that Apple plans to add back in the future.

Custom feeds are still supported for Apple’s Podcasts app on iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, Apple Vision Pro, and Mac with the OS 27 updates.

tvOS 27 is only compatible with the second- and third-generation Apple TV 4K. The original Apple TV 4K is capped at tvOS 26 — which still supports custom URL feeds.

title: Possible Google device at FCC could be Wear OS-powered fitness tracker
snippet: A new piece of hardware passed through FCC certification today, and the evidence points to it being a Wear OS-powered device made by Google. more…
fullText:
A new piece of hardware passed through FCC certification today, and the evidence points to it being a Wear OS-powered device made by Google.

This “Wireless Device” — as it’s officially labeled — comes from Goertek, which is already known for manufacturing various generations of Pixel Buds.

The “G8BL6” model name matches Google’s usual pattern for first-party hardware. Meanwhile, the e-label points to the existence of a screen, with the access method being Settings > System > Regulatory Information. That is identical to how you access the e-label on the Pixel Watch today. 

This would suggest the presence of Wear OS, with that possibility further bolstered by how the Android Debug Bridge (ADB) was leveraged during the testing process.

	

On the connectivity front, this device has Bluetooth LE and Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), or GPS. The former uses a “Metal frame Antenna.”

Taken together, G8BL6 is most likely a Google fitness tracker powered by Wear OS, though the lack of Wi-Fi is curious. This would be a new form factor for the platform, raising questions about whether the OS is battery-efficient enough.

This filing comes as an unknown Google tracker was spotted in Pixel 11 advertising this August. We saw a vertical, pill-shaped display with a Pixel Watch-esque band. The watch face is very familiar, down to the existing Wear OS complications for fitness.

Following the Fitbit Air, this would make sense as a successor to the popular Fitbit Charge line, which is currently priced at $160 and last updated in 2023.

title: Apple’s iPhone Duo foldable has the same IP68 protection as Pixel Fold – temporary
snippet: Apple did the thing. The first foldable iPhone has arrived with the new iPhone Duo delivering a pretty compelling package for interested foldable customers who don’t want to give up on iOS. It also addresses a durability gap that few others have managed with IP68 protection but, like Pixel 11 Pro Fold, that’s only a temporary rating for the iPhone Duo. more…
fullText:
Apple did the thing. The first foldable iPhone has arrived with the new iPhone Duo delivering a pretty compelling package for interested foldable customers who don’t want to give up on iOS. It also addresses a durability gap that few others have managed with IP68 protection but, like Pixel 11 Pro Fold, that’s only a temporary rating for the iPhone Duo.

In a footnote on Apple’s iPhone Duo listing, the company admits that the IP68 dust/water protection won’t last forever:

iPhone Duo is splash, water, and dust resistant and was tested under controlled laboratory conditions with a rating of IP68 under IEC standard 60529 (maximum depth of 6 meters up to 30 minutes). Splash, water, and dust resistance are not permanent conditions. Resistance might decrease as a result of normal wear…

It’s a bit less of a thought for a typical slab-style smartphone, as the dust/water resistance there shouldn’t change drastically unless there is external damage. But, with a foldable, there are moving parts to account for and, as such, the rating may wane over time.

Apple’s not alone.

	

Google was the first to manage an IP68 rating on a foldable with last year’s Pixel 10 Pro Fold, a spec that’s since carried on to the Pixel 11 Pro Fold. In Google’s own footnote, the company explains:

Designed to comply with dust and water protection rating IP68 under IEC standard 60529 when each device leaves the factory but the device is not water or dust proof. The accessories are not water or dust resistant. Water resistance and dust resistance are not permanent conditions and will diminish or be lost over time due to normal wear and tear, device repair, disassembly or damage. Phone is not drop/tumble proof and dropping your device may result in loss of water/dust resistance.

As pointed out in our comments, Google also carries the same disclaimer on standard Pixel phones, but the same isn’t true of every brand. Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro listings, for example, don’t mention anything about the water resistance waning. Honor does say the same about its Magic V6 foldable, with the IP68/69 rating “not permanently effective, and the protective performance may decrease due to daily wear and tear,” with the same disclaimer on Magic 8 Pro. Foldables are still more prone to this problem than typical slab smartphones, though.

Still, it’s good to see that Apple is getting right out of the gate with IP68 on the iPhone Duo. Samsung, for comparison, still lacks the heightened dust resistance of the three devices mentioned here, with IP48 dust/water resistance on the latest Galaxy foldables.

First macOS 27 RC rolling out

With the official release of macOS 27 Golden Gate fast approaching, Apple has now moved the operating system into the Release Candidate stage, signaling that development of the initial release is essentially complete. The macOS 27 RC is now rolling out to developers. Here are the details.

While macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 8 didn’t include any notable user-facing changes, beta 6 introduced redesigned traffic light window controls with a more Liquid Glass-like appearance.

macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces the new Siri app alongside Apple’s revamped Siri AI, as well as an AI-powered Shortcuts app that can create shortcuts from natural-language prompts. Safari also gains a prompt-based extension builder.

The update additionally includes new Golden Gate-themed wallpapers and screensavers, while restoring fixed-radius corners for windows and apps after macOS 26 introduced dynamically changing corner radii.

The release build for macOS 27 RC 1 is 26A5428. We’re digging through the release and will report back if we find anything new.

Installing macOS 27 Golden Gate RC

Here’s how to install the first macOS 27 Golden Release Candidate:

Back up your Mac

Open System Settings

Go to General ⇾ Software Update

Click the ‘i’ icon next to Beta Updates

From the dropdown menu in the top-right, select the macOS Developer Golden Gate Beta

title: Electric air taxis get the green light for test flights in Texas
snippet: A new federal program to test the feasibility of electric, hybrid-electric, and autonomous aircraft kicks off today in Texas - before the rules governing this new technology have even been finalized. Earlier this year, the Federal Aviation Administration's Advanced Air Mobility and Electric Vertical Takeoff and Landing (eVTOL) Integration Pilot Program (eIPP) selected eight state-led projects to serve as some of the first public tests of these new aircraft. The first one kicks off today in Texas, featuring three eVTOL companies: Joby, Beta, and Wisk. For the next week, these companies will conduct test flights demonstrating future routes … Read the full story at The Verge.
fullText:
A new federal program to test the feasibility of electric, hybrid-electric, and autonomous aircraft kicks off today in Texas — before the rules governing this new technology have even been finalized.

Earlier this year, the Federal Aviation Administration’s Advanced Air Mobility and Electric Vertical Takeoff and Landing (eVTOL) Integration Pilot Program (eIPP) selected eight state-led projects to serve as some of the first public tests of these new aircraft. The first one kicks off today in Texas, featuring three eVTOL companies: Joby, Beta, and Wisk.

For the next week, these companies will conduct test flights demonstrating future routes between cities and regional airports, including Dallas Fort Worth International Airport. The aircraft won’t carry any passengers, but regulators will be keen to see how the state’s air traffic control system handles the uptick in flight traffic. The companies, meanwhile, are eager to prove to the federal government that their aircraft deserve to be awarded type certification, which is required before any of them can carry passengers commercially in the US.

But type certification can take years to attain, which led to the White House to create this pilot program allowing these companies to demonstrate their new technology — even before the regulatory process has concluded. Through the eIPP, the companies hope to accelerate their path to market by getting a head start on data collection that will be needed for certification. Data from the program will also be used to “develop new regulations that safely enable this futuristic technology at scale,” the White House said earlier.

The companies say they are thrilled to demonstrate the future of electric and autonomous flight, which they argue will help reduce car traffic in cities and open up new mobility opportunities for consumers.

“I’m incredibly excited by the potential for vertical lift in Texas, a state with the infrastructure, expertise, and partnerships to help lead the next era of American aviation,” JoeBen Bevirt, Founder and CEO of Joby Aviation, said in a statement.

Several of these companies have conducted public test flights before — Joby’s egg-shaped aircraft demonstrated its future route between Lower Manhattan and JFK Airprot earlier this year — but these will be the first official flights under the White House’s new pilot program. Additional tests are being planned in New York, Utah, Pennsylvania, Louisiana, Florida, North Carolina, and New Mexico.

Legal in-fighting, however, could muddy the picture for electric aviation. Joby and one of its rivals, Archer, are currently suing each other for stolen trade secrets and corporate espionage. Technology limitations, including battery weight and sensor decisions, could also hamper the rollout.

A new federal program to test the feasibility of electric, hybrid-electric, and autonomous aircraft kicks off today in Texas — before the rules governing this new technology have even been finalized.

Earlier this year, the Federal Aviation Administration’s Advanced Air Mobility and Electric Vertical Takeoff and Landing (eVTOL) Integration Pilot Program (eIPP) selected eight state-led projects to serve as some of the first public tests of these new aircraft. The first one kicks off today in Texas, featuring three eVTOL companies: Joby, Beta, and Wisk.

title: Motorola briefly teases ‘Signature 27’ phone, hints it might come to the US
snippet: Motorola hasn’t had a proper flagship in the US in quite some time, but a brief appearance of “Signature 27” hints that might change in the coming months. more…
fullText:
Motorola hasn’t had a proper flagship in the US in quite some time, but a brief appearance of “Signature 27” hints that might change in the coming months.

The Motorola Signature launched in early 2026 as the first big launch in quite a while that (mostly) fits the “flagship” bill. High-end materials, solid specs, and no slouch in software updates either. It was fairly compelling, but never saw a US debut. 

For a brief little while earlier this week, Motorola’s website was showing a banner teasing the “Signature 27,” an apparent successor to the initial Signature release. The banner was spotted by Reddit users as well as GSMArena, with the single image (above) showing a large camera lens and the name of the device, and nothing else. 

The notable thing here is that the same banner also appeared on the US site, as the folks over at Android Authority noticed, with the tagline “a new perspective is coming” underneath. There’s little here to confirm it’s coming to the US market, but it’s hard to imagine any other reason for this to show up on the US site at all. 

	

The banner has since vanished across all of Motorola’s sites, suggesting it was probably posted too early. The first Motorola Signature launched in January, and the “Signature 27” name alone suggests this one is at least a couple more months away from launch.

title: How to fast charge iPhone 18 Pro
snippet: The new iPhone 18 Pro has much better battery life than its predecessors, but it also has even faster wired charging. To fast charge the new iPhone, Apple says you need to use its dynamic 40-watt power adapter with 60-watt max output and USB-C cable. With this combination, you will charge at the maximum possible speed, which is about 33% faster than previous pro iPhones could. more…
fullText:
The new iPhone 18 Pro has much better battery life than its predecessors, but it also has even faster wired charging.

To fast charge the new iPhone, Apple says you need to use its dynamic 40-watt power adapter with 60-watt max output and USB-C cable. With this combination, you will charge at the maximum possible speed, which is about 33% faster than previous pro iPhones could. 

Maximum charging speed on iPhone 18 Pro with a 60-watt charger means you can charge from zero to 50% in about 15 minutes. That’s about 5 minutes faster than iPhone 17 Pro, for comparison.

Also, at that faster charging rate, Apple says users can get about 6 hours of video playback time with just a quick five minute top-up charge.

Specifically, Apple’s specs for the new iPhone 18 fast charging times require a 60-watt USB PD 3.1-compatible power adapter with Adjustable Voltage Supply feature. Right now, the only charger readily available that meets those requirements is the Apple 40W dynamic power adapter.

When we get the phones in our hands, we’ll be able to do some hands-on battery charge time tests with other third-party adapters to see how they fare. For instance, the MacBook charger you already own will likely be rated for 96W or 140W, but it lacks the Adjustable Voltage Supply feature. 

There are also a bunch of third-party chargers rated above 40-watts, like this Anker 45W brick. Presumably, iPhone 18 Pro will achieve the same as iPhone 17 Pro did here, fast charging from empty to 50% in about twenty minutes. This is still very fast charging when you are in a pinch.

For wireless charging, iPhone 18 Pro can go from 0 to 50% in about 30 minutes when paired with the Apple MagSafe Charger and any 35-watt power brick.

iPhone 18 Pro goes up for preorder this Saturday, with first units shipping on September 18. When Apple’s foldable iPhone Duo ships next month, it will also support the same faster charging speeds as iPhone 18 Pro, if you have the right accessories as described above. 

Remember, Apple doesn’t include power bricks with their phones anymore — just a USB-C cable.

title: Apple now accepting App Store submissions built for iOS 27, macOS 27, more
snippet: Developers can now submit apps built for iOS 27 and Apple’s other new operating system releases, ahead of their official rollout next Monday. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Developers can now submit apps built for iOS 27 and Apple’s other new operating system releases, ahead of their official rollout next Monday. Here are the details.

Developers can now submit iOS 27-ready apps

During yesterday’s “Surprise and Shine” event, Apple confirmed that iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, tvOS 27, visionOS 27, and watchOS 27 will launch next Monday, September 14.

Today, Apple announced that developers can now download the Xcode 27 Release Candidate and submit apps and games built with the latest SDKs for approval.

Apple also took the opportunity to remind developers that macOS 27 will only support software built for Apple silicon:

Optimize your app for macOS 27. macOS 26 is the final release supporting Intel Mac computers and Rosetta — macOS 27 will be Apple silicon only. To limit your app to Macs with Apple silicon, set your Xcode build architecture to arm64 only, then rebuild and resubmit. Removing support for Intel-based apps lets you further simplify your development and optimize your app for Apple silicon.

Additionally, Apple reminded developers to answer the new age rating questions required for features such as Time Allowances, and encouraged them to prepare their App Store listings for the new product page headers and search result assets, with updated design guidance and templates available for product pages, screenshots, app previews, and In-App Events.

Finally, Apple reaffirmed that “starting April 2027, apps and games uploaded to App Store Connect need to meet the following minimum requirements”:

iOS and iPadOS apps must be built with the iOS 27 & iPadOS 27 SDK or later

tvOS apps must be built with the tvOS 27 SDK or later

visionOS apps must be built with the visionOS 27 SDK or later

watchOS apps must be built with the watchOS 27 SDK or later

title: Apple announces A20 Pro chip with 2nm design and major performance gains
snippet: Apple today unveiled the A20 Pro, its first chip built on 2nm technology at its “Surprise and Shine” event, bringing major CPU, GPU, and AI upgrades to the iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro, and iPhone 18 Pro Max. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple today unveiled the A20 Pro, its first chip built on 2nm technology at its “Surprise and Shine” event, bringing major CPU, GPU, and AI upgrades to the iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro, and iPhone 18 Pro Max. Here are the details.

Apple announces A20 Pro chip

Apple today unveiled the A20 Pro chip, which will power the iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max.

The A20 Pro features a new architecture built on 2nm technology, with smaller and more densely packed transistors that Apple says enable upgrades across the entire chip.

The new A20 Pro chip packs six CPU cores, featuring two supercores that Apple says are 20% faster, alongside four efficiency cores. All are integrated with neural accelerators for low-latency AI workloads.

The A20 Pro’s GPU has a seven-core design, which Apple says enables up to a 40% performance increase. Apple also introduced a new version of its neural accelerators, with 2x faster 8-bit floating-point math, aimed at advanced AI workloads such as running third-party LLMs on-device.

The Neural Engine has also been upgraded with a second engine, bringing the total to 32 cores and delivering twice the compute performance.

Apple says these CPU, GPU, and Neural Engine improvements are supported by a 50% increase in memory bandwidth, enabled by what it calls the widest memory interface ever shipped in an iPhone.

The A20 Pro also introduces a new packaging design inspired by Apple’s M-series chips, placing the silicon die side by side with the memory. According to Apple, this removes the memory from the SoC’s thermal path and allows the silicon to connect directly to its next-generation vapor chamber, significantly improving thermal performance.

To support the iPhone Duo’s dual-display design, the A20 Pro also features a new display engine that drives both displays simultaneously and enables smooth transitions between them.

Apple says it also blends the unique pixel layout around the under-display camera area of the iPhone Duo to deliver a consistent visual experience.
